posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
The day closed at 233 feeder visits, well above the recent weekly average of 63.6. Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees account for the vast majority of visual records.

As the light faded, the auditory log shifted away from the heavy Carolina Wren presence. The final hours brought a quieter mix, ending with a Northern Cardinal and a Carolina Wren vocalizing near dusk. These last sounds preceded the day’s final visual record: a Ruby-throated Hummingbird detected at the exact moment of sunset.

The physical presence remained consistent until the very end, with a Tufted Titmouse still perched on the tube seed feeder and a Blue Jay near the ground. This closes the day’s log, capping a period of sustained activity that far exceeded the recent baseline.
